decisions.where: README.md: the opening names the colleague from accounting who bills clients from Excel and writes no Python; the first item of Requirements names the developer who does the setup; the Walkthrough holds accounting's everyday steps.
README.md has no License section and names no license, and no LICENSE file is added.
README.md, Walkthrough: the rows in Excel as a table, what accounting types, and the invoice printed for the same rows at 19% and at 7.7%, from a real run.

README.md, Requirements and Installation: the developer, signed in as the colleague, checks Python by py --version, runs py -m pip install --user pipx, py -m pipx ensurepath and py -m pipx install of the main.zip URL, and sees in a new PowerShell window that invoicer --help prints its usage line. The everyday steps follow in the Walkthrough, with no Python in them.

README.md, Walkthrough: the once-only Excel setting of a point as the decimal separator in File > Options > Advanced; then one invoice line in each row as description, price, quantity in columns A to C, no heading row, a discount as a negative price, saved as CSV UTF-8 under the name lines.csv. How it works, Does Excel save the rows the way invoicer reads them: the semicolons come from the Windows list separator, and how to set it.
README.md: Requirements and Installation use py and PowerShell on Windows; the Walkthrough uses the menus of Microsoft 365 Excel, File Explorer's Open in Terminal, and PowerShell.

settled.ground: pyproject.toml says to install by pipx from a path or URL of the repository. lovaizu/playground is public, so its main.zip URL needs no Git on the accounting laptop. A try from the pushed branch's zip installed invoicer 1.5.0. The URL works once this pull request is merged into main.

settled.point: whose Windows account the setup is done in
settled.decided: The developer signs in to Windows as the colleague from accounting, and whoami shows it
settled.ground: pipx installs the command and adds it to PATH for the signed-in Windows account only, so a setup done in the developer's own account leaves the colleague without the command.

settled.decided: invoicer makes no PDF; adds no client name, invoice number or date; shows every amount in euros only; and takes one tax rate for the whole invoice
settled.ground: Each is what a reader of an invoice tool would count on, and invoicer as the person signed it off doesn't do it: render.py prints text with EUR fixed, and command.py takes one --rate and no client details. A reader who needs any of them decides against it before starting.

settled.decided: Right-click the folder that holds lines.csv in File Explorer, choose Open in Terminal, and type invoicer lines.csv --rate 19
settled.ground: Open in Terminal opens PowerShell in that folder on Windows 11, so accounting types the file name alone, with no path to type.

settled.point: the doubts that How it works answers
settled.decided: Are the totals right to the cent; what if a row or the tax rate is wrong; does Excel save the rows the way invoicer reads them
settled.ground: These are the doubts that decide whether accounting trusts the invoice and can work without a developer. totals.py rounds each amount half up to the cent and adds the printed amounts. command.py refuses a wrong row or rate, naming it. lines.py reads semicolons and a decimal point.

settled.decided: The issues of lovaizu/playground, for the developers
settled.ground: The repository has no docs folder or changelog, and its issues are on. Accounting asks no developer for the everyday steps, and a fault of invoicer goes to the developers there.
